chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

When you face the qiblah with your face, then do not turn your face away from the qiblah, lest you invalidate your salat (prayer), for Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the obligatory prayer:
"So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it."
And lower your gaze in humility, and do not raise it toward the sky; rather, let it be in front of your face at the place of your sajdah (prostration).

key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the sky, toward which one is told not to raise the gaze
key_terms.سُجُودِكَ: your place of prostration in salat (prayer)
key_terms.صَلَاتَكَ: your salat (prayer), whose validity is being discussed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about facing the qiblah and lowering the gaze during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the worshipper to maintain proper orientation toward the qiblah during salat (prayer) and not turn the face away in a manner that invalidates the prayer. It also emphasizes khushuʿ through lowering the gaze and keeping one’s sight fixed on the place of sajdah, while grounding this practice in the Qur'anic command to face al-Masjid al-Ḥarām.
